memory_candidates: Lean 4 Finset-exclusion induction gotcha: when parametrizing an induction with an explicit `excl : Finset` to carve out a branch the caller already owns, the edge-conjunct's membership check must be on the edge's TARGET, not its SOURCE. Checking the source lets the boundary edge INTO the excluded branch (source outside, target inside) fall under the obligation, which is generally unprovable if the underlying relation has no 'raise-source-only, keep-target-exact' primitive (here `cs5FCIncest`). Checking the target correctly excludes exactly that boundary edge (and everything inside the excluded closure), deferring it to the caller's own separately-established fact.

Lean 4 pattern: `Relation.ReflTransGen.head`/`.tail`/`.cases_head`/`.cases_tail` do NOT support dot-notation when the first explicit argument's type is a plain relation fact (e.g. `G.R a b`) rather than a `ReflTransGen` fact itself -- `hab.head hbc` fails with 'Invalid field notation' since `hab : G.R a b` has head symbol `G.R`, not `Relation.ReflTransGen`. Must call fully-qualified: `Relation.ReflTransGen.head hab hbc`.

Lean 4 `subst` direction gotcha (generalizes prior ReflTransGen-cases lessons): `subst h` for `h : a = b` eliminates whichever variable is on the side Lean judges eliminable, and for two plain local variables this can eliminate the OLDER/outer-scoped one (e.g. `subst huzeq` for `huzeq : u = z` eliminated `z`, not `u`, breaking every subsequent reference to `z` within that same tactic block with 'unknown identifier'). When both sides are local variables used elsewhere in the SAME tactic block, prefer `rw [h] at otherHyp` over `subst h` to avoid unpredictably renaming an outer variable out of existence.

CSLib tree-cascade lifting lemma pattern (task 537 Phase 7, Simpson 8.1.3): split into (1) a downward-cascade helper (raise a node + its full forward-reachable closure through a chosen Finset of un-excluded direct children, well-founded on a rank-based Set.ncard measure) and (2) a Finset-exclusion-parametrized ancestor-walk induction (walk up the unique-parent chain, at each ancestor invoking the downward helper for the un-excluded sibling branches, combining via an if-then-else on ReflTransGen-reachability from the current node). A small reusable 'siblings_disjoint' lemma (distinct children of a common parent have disjoint forward-reachable closures, via unique-parent + graded-rank) is needed by BOTH the downward helper's own combine step and the ancestor-walk's exclusion-identity conjunct -- worth factoring out as a standalone theorem rather than reproving inline twice.
